claim: No priority claim is made for Test Cover, submodularity ratio, adaptive submodularity, critical-node/network-interdiction optimization, or graph connectivity under deletion. The project-specific object is a truth-rooted, response-induced deletion family coupled to connected approximate inverse fibers.

references.citation: K.M.J. de Bontridder et al., Approximation algorithms for the test cover problem, Mathematical Programming 98 (2003) 477-492.
references.overlap: Selecting tests so every item pair is distinguished is exactly the finite pair-separation objective used here when tests are thresholded pair separators.
references.difference: It does not encode a declared topology or only the truth-rooted connected survivor component.

references.citation: Abhimanyu Das and David Kempe, Submodular Meets Spectral, ICML 2011.
references.overlap: Introduces submodularity ratio as a quantitative diagnostic for greedy performance beyond exact submodularity.
references.difference: Their regression/subset-selection objective is different; M2 reports a restricted finite-budget ratio only as a diagnostic, not a theorem transfer.

references.citation: Daniel Golovin and Andreas Krause, Adaptive Submodularity: Theory and Applications in Active Learning and Stochastic Optimization, JAIR 42 (2011) 427-486.
references.overlap: Framework for adaptive greedy guarantees under uncertain outcomes.
references.difference: M2 is static known-outcome conditioning on a fixed truth. No adaptive-submodularity claim is made.

references.citation: Bernardetta Addis, Marco Di Summa, Andrea Grosso, Identifying critical nodes in undirected graphs: Complexity results and polynomial algorithms for bounded treewidth, Discrete Applied Mathematics 161 (2013) 2349-2360.
references.overlap: Deletes budgeted graph nodes to reduce connectivity; establishes hardness and tractable bounded-treewidth structure for established connectivity metrics.
references.difference: M2 selects experiments, each inducing a set of inconsistent worlds, and scores only the truth-containing component.

references.citation: Siqian Shen and J. Cole Smith, Polynomial-time algorithms for solving a class of critical node problems on trees and series-parallel graphs, Networks 60 (2012) 103-119.
references.overlap: Shows graph structure beyond trees matters for exact connectivity-deletion optimization.
references.difference: Their objectives include number/largest size of components, not the response-induced truth-rooted set function used here.

references.citation: Kevin T. Kennedy et al., Nodal interdiction, Mathematical and Computer Modelling 54 (2011) 3116-3125.
references.overlap: Direct node-removal formulation in network interdiction.
references.difference: Generic interdiction is broader; it does not imply submodularity or the M2 exact grid counterexample.
